title: Certified Interpolation Oversampling: Per-Instance Safety Guarantees for Imbalanced Learning
multiclass data reduced to two classes?: yes, p.15 §5.1 and Table 1 p.16: smallest class vs rest (Waveform, Statlog Landsat, Page Blocks, Letter); KEEL 'x vs y' and one-vs-rest sets (e.g. glass-0-1-2-3 vs 4-5-6, yeast-2 vs 4, ecoli4)
seed selection changed? (y/n, page): y, p.8 §4.2 Eq.(9): anchor drawn from P_alpha(i) ∝ (eps0 + s_i)^alpha, s_i = safety score (Eq.(8) p.8); locked alpha = +2 (p.25)
sample allocation changed? (y/n, page): y, p.8 Eq.(9) and Alg.1 lines 7-8 p.14: anchor redrawn for each synthetic point until ΔN = N0−N1; expected count per anchor ΔN·P_alpha(i)
neighbour choice changed? (y/n, page): y, p.11 §4.3 Eq.(11): two distinct endpoints drawn without replacement from the k minority NN, weights = (eps0 + neighbour clearance) × q-Gaussian locality
placement rule changed? (y/n, page): y, p.12 §4.4 Eqs.(12)-(14): point on the segment joining the two neighbours (anchor is not an endpoint); lambda from a truncated q-Gaussian centred at mu_i
post-filtering changed? (y/n, page): n, Alg.1 p.14: returns D ∪ S_syn, no removal step
inside a pipeline? (y/n, page): n, Alg.1 p.14; §5.1 and §5.3 pp.15-17: run once per training fold before the classifiers
removes or moves original examples? (C3,: n, Alg.1 line 17 p.14: D' = D ∪ S_syn
adaptive choice of k? (y/n, page): n, §5.5 p.17: k in {5,7} fixed once on a disjoint tuning suite; Alg.1 line 1 p.14 only truncates k to min(k, N1−1, N0)
notes: Year from arXiv id 2501.15790 (file is v2 dated 6 Aug 2026, p.1). Core: convex combination of two minority neighbours of the anchor, "Two endpoints, rather than one neighbor as in SMOTE" (p.11). Binarization: "Multi-class datasets are binarized by the smallest-class-versus-rest rule" (p.15). Seed and allocation both y because one distribution P_alpha drives both; alpha = 0 gives uniform seeding (Lemma 2, p.9). Per-anchor median bandwidth h_i (Eq.(10) p.10) adapts scale, not k. Locked k not stated in the text.

title: Geometric SMOTE a geometrically enhanced drop-in replacement for SMOTE
multiclass data reduced to two classes?: yes, Table 1 pp.17-18: multiclass sources appear as one class vs rest (e.g. IRIS 50 vs 100, WINE 71 vs 107, GLASS 70 vs 144, VEHICLE 199 vs 647, SEGMENTATION 330 vs 1980); the reduction rule is not described
seed selection changed? (y/n, page): n, §4.1 p.8 and step 3 p.9: S_min shuffled and every minority instance used in turn as centre
sample allocation changed? (y/n, page): n, §4.1 p.8 and steps 2-3 p.9: cycles through shuffled S_min until N points (equal per seed up to the remainder)
neighbour choice changed? (y/n, page): y, Alg.1 p.7, §4.2 pp.8-9, step 4 pp.9-11: surface point via alpha_sel: minority (random one of k minority NN, as SMOTE), majority (nearest majority NN) or combined (closer of the two)
placement rule changed? (y/n, page): y, Alg.1 p.7, Eqs.(1)-(8) p.9, steps 6-9 pp.12-15: uniform point in a unit hyperball, truncated (alpha_trunc) and deformed to a hyper-spheroid (alpha_def), translated to x_center and scaled by R = ||x_center − x_surface||
post-filtering changed? (y/n, page): n, Alg.1 p.7: every x_gen is added to S_gen
inside a pipeline? (y/n, page): n, §5.4.1 p.19: generated from the training folds before training the classifier
removes or moves original examples? (C3,: n, §5.4.1 p.19: training set = T_i ∪ T_g,i
adaptive choice of k? (y/n, page): n, §5.4.1 pp.19-20: k in {3,5} as one axis of a hyper-parameter grid
notes: Printed page numbers used (pdf page = printed + 1 because of a cover sheet). Core: region built around the seed-surface segment, "G-SMOTE extends the linear interpolation mechanism by introducing a geometric region" (p.9). SMOTE is a special case: "reproduces the SMOTE algorithm is αdef = 1.0, αtrunc = 1.0 and αsel = minority" (p.23). alpha_trunc < 0 extrapolates away from the surface point ('Inverse SMOTE', p.23); with alpha_sel = majority/combined the far endpoint can be a majority instance. Multiclass reduction inferred from Table 1 counts only.

title: Loyalty-SMOTE: Data synthesis algorithm for effective imbalanced data classification
multiclass data reduced to two classes?: yes for the binary groups: Table 2 p.8 includes binarized multiclass sources (KEEL glass5, vowel0, ecoli-0-1-3-7_vs_2-6, ecoli-0-1-4-6_vs_5, yeast-0-3-5-9_vs_7-8; iris, bezediris), rule not described; no for group 4 (Table 5 p.8; §4.4.4 p.12)
seed selection changed? (y/n, page): y, §3.3 p.6 and Fig.3 Step 3 p.5: seeds = minority boundary samples with 0 ≤ Loyalty ≤ m (m = 0.5, Table 8 p.9); signed samples with Loyalty < 0 excluded (§3.2 p.5; Fig.2 p.4)
sample allocation changed? (y/n, page): n, §3.3 p.6: SMOTE run on the boundary set until balance; no per-seed weighting (Table 8 p.9 'Sampling ratio = 2' not explained)
neighbour choice changed? (y/n, page): n, §3.3 p.6, Fig.3 line 20 p.5, Table 8 p.9: standard SMOTE with k = 5; neighbour pool apparently limited to the boundary set / non-signed samples (not stated explicitly)
post-filtering changed? (y/n, page): y, §3.4 pp.6-7 and Fig.3 Step 4 p.5: after generation Loyalty is recomputed; signed minority samples still < 0 removed; signed majority samples removed by an LOF rule
inside a pipeline? (y/n, page): n, §4.3 p.10: data-level step before an SVM
removes or moves original examples? (C3,: y, §3.4 p.6: signed original samples deleted; §3.2 pp.5-6: in multiclass data unloyal samples are relabelled to the class with the highest Attraction
adaptive choice of k? (y/n, page): n, Table 8 p.9: k = 9 (Loyalty) and k = 5 (SMOTE) fixed; k only varied in a sensitivity study (Fig.9 p.7, §4.4.2 p.10)
notes: Variants: binary branch (signing, §3.2 p.5) = B; multiclass branch (Attraction relabelling) = M; paper = B+M. FLAG: in multiclass sets "the class with the fewest instances is considered the minority class" (p.12), so only one class seems to be oversampled (Fig.3 line 19 'If class is minority'). Relabelling: "assign these samples to the class with the highest Attraction" (p.6). FLAG: cleaning rule inconsistent: text p.4/p.6 and Fig.3 say LOF < 0 (impossible for LOF), Fig.2 p.4 says LOF > 1; Fig.3 recomputes Loyalty for every sample, the text only for signed minority samples; Fig.3 line 13 removes noise in Step 2 while the text (p.5) says unloyal samples are retained.

title: RAMOBoost: Ranked Minority Oversampling in Boosting
multiclass data reduced to two classes?: yes, p.1630 and Table II p.1631: one class vs rest (Vehicle van, Segment brickface, Letter Z, Glass 6, ...), merged classes (Texture 13+14; Page_blocks 4 classes vs text), class pairs with the other classes dropped (Abalone 18 vs 9; Yeast POX vs CYT)
seed selection changed? (y/n, page): y, Alg.1 steps 2-4 p.1627, Eqs.(2)-(3): seeds sampled from the minority subset e2 with r_i = 1/(1+exp(−alpha·delta_i)), delta_i = majority count among the k1 NN; every minority example keeps some weight (p.1628)
sample allocation changed? (y/n, page): y, Alg.1 steps 4-5 p.1627 and §III-C p.1628: more synthetic points for examples with more majority neighbours; N = 200% of the minority per iteration (p.1635)
neighbour choice changed? (y/n, page): n, Alg.1 step 5 p.1627; §III-C-1 p.1628: random one of the k2 nearest minority neighbours (Euclidean) in e2; k2 = 10 (p.1635)
placement rule changed? (y/n, page): n, §III-C-1 p.1628: x_i + random[0,1] × (x_hat − x_i), as SMOTE
post-filtering changed? (y/n, page): n, Alg.1 p.1627: nothing removed after generation
inside a pipeline? (y/n, page): y, Alg.1 p.1627: generation inside every AdaBoost.M2 iteration (T = 20, p.1635); each base learner gets S_e plus N new synthetic points
removes or moves original examples? (C3,: y, Alg.1 step 1 p.1627: each base learner trains on S_e, a D_t-weighted resample of identical size, so originals can be missing or duplicated (judgement call, see notes)
adaptive choice of k? (y/n, page): n, §IV-C p.1635: k1 = 5 and k2 = 10 fixed (alpha = 0.3 chosen by cross-validation)
notes: Two-class: "we also consider only two-class imbalanced problems in our current study" (p.1630). Seeds weighted, not restricted: "considers all minority examples for synthetic generation, albeit at varied levels" (p.1628). C3 = y only because of boosting by resampling: "get back the sampled dataset Se of identical size" (Alg.1 step 1, p.1627); there is no cleaning step, so code n if per-round resampling is not counted. Neighbour pool is e2 (minority part of the resample), not the original minority set.

title: A Study of the Behavior of Several Methods for Balancing Machine Learning Training Data
multiclass data reduced to two classes?: yes, §5 p.24 and Table 3 p.25: class with fewest examples as positive, remainder collapsed as negative; Letter and Splice each split into two sets (Letter-a, Letter-vowel = all vowels vs rest, Splice-ie, Splice-ei)
sample allocation changed? (y/n, page): n, p.25: Smote amount set until classes are balanced; per-seed rule unchanged
neighbour choice changed? (y/n, page): n, §4.3 p.23: Smote unchanged; Smote k not stated; their k-NN uses HVDM (Euclidean for numeric, VDM for nominal attributes) (§4.2 p.22)
post-filtering changed? (y/n, page): y, §4.3 pp.23-24: after Smote, examples of both classes forming Tomek links are removed (Smote+Tomek) or ENN removes every example misclassified by its 3 NN (Smote+ENN)
inside a pipeline? (y/n, page): n, §5 pp.24-25: balancing applied to the training data, then C4.5
removes or moves original examples? (C3,: y, §4.3 p.24: Tomek-link and ENN cleaning delete original (and synthetic) examples of both classes
adaptive choice of k? (y/n, page): n, §4.3 p.24: ENN uses three nearest neighbours; Smote k not stated
notes: Two proposed SMOTE variants, both B: Smote+Tomek and Smote+ENN (CNN+Tomek, also proposed, generates nothing). Reduction: "we chose the class with fewer examples as the positive class, and collapsed the remainder" (p.24). ENN: "any example that is misclassified by its three nearest neighbors is removed" (p.24). Tomek used as cleaning: "examples from both classes are removed" (p.24). Smote+Tomek was first used in the authors' earlier bioinformatics work (p.24). Printed page numbers (pdf p.1 = p.20).
